meta.title: ErtisAuth: Open Source Identity and Access Management API
meta.description: Lightweight, self-hosted identity and access management: multi-tenant memberships, JWT tokens, fine-grained permissions and .NET SDK.

hero.title: Identity and Access Management
hero.subtitle: The right identity, the right access, stronger security
hero.description: ErtisAuth, delivers centralized, scalable, and secure identity and access management across your entire application ecosystem. From web and native applications to mobile apps and APIs, manage authentication, authorization, tokens, memberships, roles, granular & flexible permissions, dynamic user type management and OAuth integrations from a single platform.
hero.terminalTitle: Sign in and get a token

diagram.label: How ErtisAuth fits in: applications send requests to ErtisAuth and get tokens back, and ErtisAuth keeps its data in database

lightweight.title: Lightweight
lightweight.text: One service, one database. No JVM, no separate admin server, no SQL migrations.

apiFirst.title: API first
apiFirst.text: Memberships, users, roles, providers and hooks are managed through the same REST API that issues the tokens.

multiTenant.title: Multi-tenant
multiTenant.text: Each membership operates as a fully isolated environment, allowing you to securely manage multiple channels and product ecosystems under a single service—without compromising separation or security.

open.title: Free and open
open.text: MIT licensed. No per-user pricing, no feature tiers, your data stays in your database.

features.title: Everything an identity service needs
features.description: From the first sign-in to webhooks on every event, ErtisAuth covers the whole account lifecycle.

tokens.title: Tokens and sessions
tokens.text: JWT bearer tokens for users and Basic tokens for applications, refresh tokens that are single-use by default, revocation per session or for all devices, and scoped tokens limited to a subset of permissions.

memberships.title: Memberships
memberships.text: Isolated tenants, each with its own users, roles, applications, secret key, token lifetimes and mail settings.

permissions.title: RBAC and UBAC
permissions.text: Roles with permissions and forbidden rules, plus per-user and per-application overrides. The same model protects your own APIs.

providers.title: External providers
providers.text: Sign in with Google, Apple (web and native), Facebook and Microsoft. Provider tokens are validated on the server, never trusted from the client.

userTypes.title: Dynamic user types
userTypes.text: Define custom user fields with a JSON schema at runtime: validation, default values, unique fields and inheritance, without changing code.

devices.title: Device sign-in
devices.text: A code flow for smart TVs, kiosks and CLI tools: the device shows a short code, a signed-in user approves it, the device gets a token.

lifecycle.title: Account lifecycle
lifecycle.text: Email activation, password reset with single-use tokens, one-time passwords, and freezing an account to revoke all of its tokens at once.

passwords.title: Modern password hashing
passwords.text: Argon2id and PBKDF2, chosen per membership. Legacy algorithms are still supported, so existing user databases can be imported.

events.title: Events and hooks
events.text: Every operation is recorded as an event. Webhooks call your endpoints from a background queue, and mail hooks send templated emails.

operations.title: Ready for production
operations.text: OpenAPI reference with Scalar, Prometheus metrics, Application Insights, health checks and a Docker image that runs as a non-root user.

permissions.title: Four segments, any resource
permissions.description: A permission is an expression that names who may do what on which resource. Wildcards and shorter forms keep roles short, and the same expressions protect your own services.

segments.subject: Who performs the action: a user or application id
segments.resource: The type of resource, e.g. users or orders
segments.action: create, read, update, delete or a custom action
segments.object: The id of a single resource

order.ubac: A matching user or application permission decides first, whether it grants or forbids.
order.role: Otherwise the role decides, and a forbidden rule of the role always wins.
order.self: Users may still read and update their own record, unless the role forbids it.
order.scopes: A scoped token must also cover the request with its scopes.

security.title: Secure defaults, built in
security.description: An identity service is only as safe as its defaults. These protections are part of ErtisAuth and on from the start, with nothing to switch on.

items.hashing: Argon2id or PBKDF2 password hashing, chosen per membership
items.providers: Provider tokens are checked with the provider on the server, and an unverified email never links an existing account
items.refresh: Refresh tokens are single-use by default
items.sessions: Changing a password signs the user out on every other device

items.memberships: A token of one membership is rejected by every other membership
items.roles: Users and applications without a role are denied, never allowed by default
items.scopes: Scoped tokens can't reach beyond their scopes
items.secretKey: Each membership signs its tokens with its own secret key of at least 32 bytes
items.queires: All queries run solely within an isolated space specific to their own membership.

items.hidden: Password hashes and secrets can't be read, filtered or sorted on
items.errors: Unexpected errors return a generic message; the details stay in the logs
items.events: Event records and webhooks don't carry tokens or secrets

items.random: One-time passwords and device codes come from a cryptographically secure generator
items.otp: One-time passwords are single-use and limited in attempts
items.devices: Device sign-in keeps the polling secret apart from the code the user types, and stores it hashed
items.applications: Each application has its own secret, which can be rotated

yourPart.title: Your part
yourPart.text: TLS, rate limiting on public endpoints and network access to MongoDB belong to your gateway and infrastructure.

developers.title: Protect your APIs with attributes
developers.description: ErtisAuth.Sdk is a typed client for the ErtisAuth API. ErtisAuth.Sdk.AspNetCore adds authentication and permission checks to your own ASP.NET Core services.

points.attributes: Declare the resource, action and object with attributes; placeholders read route values, query parameters, headers and environment variables.
points.analyzer: A bundled Roslyn analyzer reports invalid permission attributes at compile time.
points.anyLanguage: Not on .NET? Every feature is a REST endpoint, so services in any language can verify tokens and check permissions.

developers.comment: Reached only when the caller's token grants *.orders.read.'{id}'

compare.title: Somewhere between a library and a platform
compare.description: ErtisAuth is a central, ready-to-run server like the big platforms, but small enough to run next to your own services.

keycloak.name: Keycloak
keycloak.text: A full-featured server, but a heavy Java application configured mostly through its admin console. ErtisAuth keeps the realm idea (memberships) in a small .NET service configured entirely through its API.

hosted.name: Auth0, Okta and hosted services
hosted.text: Managed for you, but paid per active user, and your user data lives on a third-party platform. ErtisAuth is self-hosted: the data stays in your MongoDB.

duende.name: Duende IdentityServer
duende.text: A framework to build your own server with, and most companies need a commercial license. ErtisAuth is a ready-to-run server under the MIT license.

identity.name: ASP.NET Core Identity
identity.text: A library embedded in each application. ErtisAuth is a central service: many applications, in any language, share the same users and permissions.

start.title: Running in a few minutes
start.description: Start ErtisAuth and MongoDB with Docker Compose, create the first membership with the one-time setup endpoint, and sign in.

run.title: Start the containers
run.text: From the root of the repository. The API listens on port 9716, the API reference is at /docs.

setup.title: Set up the installation
setup.text: Insert a setup token into the database, then call /setup once to create the first membership, role and administrator.

token.title: Get your first token
token.text: Sign in with the administrator and use the access token on any endpoint.

cta.title: Contributing to the community
